question: What site-scoped fish and diet evidence does the 2025-2026 Flowerhorn source pair support for Lake Sampaloc, and which claims remain unsuitable for a public species record?

site.registryCrosswalk: Matches the existing source-named Lake Sampaloc research lead. This source review does not validate a lake boundary, coordinates, or administrative geometry.
site.reportedHabitat: Lake and shallow vegetated shoreline areas; the article describes the fish as freshwater, but the waterbody salinity field remains unassessed in Bangwit's scope.
site.observationWindow: The article references an on-site survey but does not state its field dates in the pages reviewed. A caretaker interview is dated August 2025.
site.samplingScope: Qualitative field observations, local reports, and a caretaker interview; no fish sampling frame, gear, standardized effort, station allocation, or voucher crosswalk is reported in the reviewed article pages.

sourceReportedLabels.labelAsReported: Flowerhorn / Midas cichlids (Amphilophus spp.; later described as hybrids)
sourceReportedLabels.evidenceType: Qualitative author field observations and local/caretaker reports from Lake Sampaloc, including shallow vegetated areas and fish-pen context.
sourceReportedLabels.limits: Amphilophus spp. and Flowerhorn hybrid/cultivar wording do not resolve a binomial species identity. No voucher, sequence, diagnostic table, count, or standardized abundance estimate was reviewed.

sourceReportedLabels.evidenceType: Named in the article's field/local-report narrative and figure caption.
sourceReportedLabels.limits: Retain only as the authors' source label; no voucher or independently verified fish identification was found. The source does not establish a complete Sampaloc species inventory.

sourceReportedLabels.evidenceType: Described as fish-pen stock in the article.
sourceReportedLabels.limits: This fish-pen context is not evidence of a wild-lake occurrence from this source.

reportedFishEvidence.interpretation: These are source-reported qualitative leads, not normalized taxon assertions, a complete checklist, quantified population trends, or proof of current catchability. The 2025 conference abstract and 2026 magazine article share the title and author team and are treated as one research lineage, not two independent studies.

unreported: The field observation dates and complete sampling period.
Fish collection or observation protocol, standardized effort, station-by-taxon allocation, sample counts, vouchers, sequences, and a machine-readable data table.
An independently validated site-level identification for the source-reported fish labels.
studyDesignLimits.proposedNotCompleted: The article's approximately 20 interviews and 10 shoreline transects are framed as a proposed rapid creel/transect study, not completed survey effort; they must not be attributed to the field observations reported in this article.

dietAndInteractionLeads.flowerhorn: Follow-up review checked the Yamamoto and Tagawa citation metadata and an official USFWS secondary summary for Amphilophus citrinellus. The book itself was not accessed, and the secondary species-specific summary is not local gut-content evidence for Lake Sampaloc Flowerhorn hybrids.
dietAndInteractionLeads.jaguarCichlid: Follow-up review confirmed that the cited Dadiono and Murti (2023) paper concerns Flowerhorn in Sempor Reservoir, Indonesia, not Parachromis managuensis or diet. A separate Agasen et al. (2006) UPLB repository abstract reports historical Taal Lake Jaguar Guapote gut-content findings; this does not establish Sampaloc diet, and the full article and reuse terms remain unverified.
dietAndInteractionLeads.productDisposition: No diet assertion or bait recommendation added. Any future natural-diet card must retain the exact taxonomic scope, source trail, context, and distinction from bait suggestions.

safetyAndPolicy.sourceStatement: The article advises against consumption pending risk assessment and discusses possible parasite and contaminant concerns.
safetyAndPolicy.limits: The reviewed source pages did not provide a Lake Sampaloc fish-tissue test or a current official public-health advisory. Do not convert the article's precautionary discussion into a Bangwit safety alert, local consumption warning, or legal rule.
safetyAndPolicy.legalLimits: The article's BFAR/LLDA permitting suggestions are not current legal advice and are not adopted as rules.

accessAndReuse.reviewedItems: Official World Aquaculture magazine pages 35-38, the official Ateneo Archium metadata/abstract page, and the World Aquaculture Society 2025 meeting abstract page.
accessAndReuse.articleAvailability: Official WAS article text pages 35-38 were reviewed. The Ateneo Archium download endpoint returned HTTP 403; no complete article PDF or images were downloaded or retained, and the complete methods/references were not independently verified.
accessAndReuse.versionRelationship: The 2025 meeting abstract and 2026 article share the same title and authors. They may be conference/article versions of the same work and are not counted as independent evidence.
accessAndReuse.rights: The WAS site footer states copyright and All Rights Reserved; no open article license or explicit Bangwit reuse grant was identified. The Archium metadata page exposed no separate item-level reuse license. No verbatim article text, table, or figure was copied into the app or review file; the review retains brief attributed summaries and citations.

nextAction: Seek method, voucher, and reuse details for the Sampaloc field observations; the Jaguar diet citation mismatch is documented and a separate historical Taal abstract-only lead is identified. Do not transfer Taal results to Sampaloc or use secondary Midas-cichlid diet summaries for unidentified hybrids.

sources.supports: Official World Aquaculture Magazine article opening page, title/authors, literature-derived diet summary, Lake Sampaloc description, and Flowerhorn group context.
Official article continuation with Lake Sampaloc fish community and field-observation discussion.
Official article continuation describing fish-pen observations, the August 2025 caretaker interview, and the stated precautionary consumption discussion.
Official article continuation distinguishing field/local reports from the proposed future transect/interview work and reporting the source's Jaguar cichlid interaction lead.
Official 2025 conference abstract with matching title and author team; retained as a related version, not independent replication.
Ateneo institutional metadata, author attribution, article date, and abstract. Its download link returned HTTP 403 in this review.
